title: Congestion latency and the approval queue bottleneck
text: Ismail and Azhar define 'congestion' as the operational failure where individual tasks accelerate dramatically while total organizational cycle time remains unchanged, because generated outputs pile up in existing human review and sign-off queues. While tracking human override rates over time can signal operational learning, a declining override rate must be evaluated against reviewer fatigue, permissive rubber-stamping, and silent escaped defects.
qualification: Operational critique and diagnostic metric. A lower override rate is not an unalloyed indicator of higher quality; it can also reflect shifting case complexity, reduced checking rigor, or narrower task delegation.
